sentences.text: This application coming on for orders this day, th e co  following:

ORDER T he applicant has filed this first application under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure,
1973 for grant of anticipatory bail.

2. Applicant apprehends his arrest in connection with Crime No.284 of 2024 registered at Police Station Hatpipliya District Dewas for the offence punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471, 409,
506, 452, 34 of IPC.
3.

As per prosecution case a written complaint has been made at P.S. Hatipipliya Distt. Dewas by complainant Rajkumar Bhatnagar alleging that the main accused Pradeep Rawal has entered into an unregistered, un-notarised and without dated sale agreement with the complainant.

It is also mentioned in the 2 MCRC-24161-2024 written complaint that prior to execution of un-registered agreement, complainant and main accused Pradeep Rawal entered into an rent agreement for the same property on 19-05-16.

As per complainant after taking sale consideration the main accused Pradeep Rawal has never executed a sale deed in favour of complainant till 2024 and on 28-12-23 Rajesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126950989/
1 the same property was sold by the main accused Pradeep Rawal to the other person namely Apoorva Jaiswal.

sentences.text: 4. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the case.
He is not concerned with the case directly or indirectly.

As per prosecution case the only allegation against the present applicant that he was the witness of earlier unregistered sale agreement except this there is no material against the present applicant.
With the aforesaid submissions, prayer for anticipatory bail is made.
5. On the other hand, learned Public Prosecutor for the respondent/State has opposed the anticipatory bail application.
The applicant is absconding since the date of registration of FIR.
Investigation is still pending and therefore, custodial interrogation may be required.

On such grounds, he prayed for its rejection.
6.

After hearing rival contentions and going through the impugned order, this Court finds that the role attributed to the applicant is only to the extent that he was a witness of the agreement and no other material is available against him.
Therefore, this Court finds that there is no need for custodial interrogation of the present applicant in the matter.

7 . Accordingly, without commenting on merits of the case, the instant application is allowed and it is directed that in the event of arrest, applicant be 3 MCRC-24161-2024 released on bail on furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One Lakh) with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Arresting Officer (Investigating Officer).
8 . The applicant shall make himself available for interrogation by the Investigating Officer as and when required.

He shall further abide by the other conditions enumerated in sub-section (2) of Section 438 of Cr.P.C.
9.
